caveats: the endpoint and the capture are local, and a keylog is only available to an operator who owns an endpoint - that is the honest precondition of this route. Without a keylog the certificate stays 'not observable' and we say so; this run shows what the same capture yields when the precondition is met.
method: real TLS 1.3 IMAPS handshake between Python ssl (OpenSSL) endpoints, captured at a relay - the same tap position as the live validation; the certificate is recovered from the encrypted handshake using the SSLKEYLOGFILE the client wrote, by deriving the handshake traffic keys (HKDF-Expand-Label, RFC 8446 s7.1) and opening the records (AES-GCM, per-record nonce from the sequence number)
server_banner: * OK [CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 AUTH=PLAIN] SecureMailScope test server
